quest.title: Great Future Star
quest.description: You've collected all six Future Stars. Time to go see Banu.
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x60, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: How's it going? Have you found all the Future Stars?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Got all six right here.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Yay! Now we can go summon the Great Future Star.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Be sure to prepare yourself before we set off! Unexpected things may happen when we summon the Great Future Star!

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Every time I attempt something special, unexpected things happen. So I'm more than well-prepared now. You should be careful, too.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: The last time I fired a Great Golden Skyscraping Arrow while at home, the yard suddenly exploded. If Apple hadn't rushed over and taken Shalmar and me away, we would've been pretty doomed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't that a bit too dangerous, actually?

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Haha. Rest assured! In general, all issues fall within acceptable bounds.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You just said that your yard exploded! That was big enough a problem if you ask Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: It'll be fine, don't worry! When you are ready, meet up with me at this location I've marked on the map. I'll be heading there first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon's got a bad feeling about this... We'd better stay alert when we get there!

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Oh! There's only one mechanism left. I must say, the final trial this time seems pretty easy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This time?

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Yup. The ones I encountered before were way more complicated than this!

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Some of them required way too many attempts to figure out the only correct solution, and some would even self-destruct if you gave the wrong solution. Painstaking — and truly troublesome!

choices.text: Why don't you take it from here?

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: Well, according to my experience, this mechanism should be no different from those basic old mechanisms Shalmar usually brings back home. You just need to insert all the keys and boom, it'll be unlocked!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Banu, have you been dealing with these weird mechanisms all this time?

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: Yes! I've been to many interesting places with Shalmar and Apple. We've had a lot of fun together!

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: In fact, we always have fun, like when I came out to look for the Future Stars this time — or whenever I came up with new settings with Shalmar or encountered situations unexpected.

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: It would be so boring to just wander around the house and do the same things every day.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon agrees! We often leave familiar places and go on adventures in new ones, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've seen many terrifying things, but we've also had many pleasant surprises — even moments that have stolen our breath away.

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: Exactly! And that's why I'm sure that we'll make great friends!

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: But, there's one thing I want you to know before we continue. I know it can get pretty dangerous playing outside in the wild, regardless of how fun it may be. That's why I've come fully prepared.

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: Shalmar told me that it's important to observe people carefully before I ask them for help and that I should stay away from the Treasure Hoarders and any Eremite strangers.

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: But you look like a nice person, which is why I asked you for help. Now that you've helped me this much, I cannot let you get hurt because of me.

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: That's my bottom line. So if you're scared, it's totally fine. I can solve this mechanism by myself.

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: That also works. Anyway, just insert the six Future Stars into the mechanism and there shouldn't be anything to worry about.

choices.text: If things can get dangerous, you'd better leave them to me.
It suddenly occurs to me that I have something else to do.

dialogues.text: Banu, are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: C'mon, there was really nothing to worry about. The book you wrote has taught me to run away if I'm no match for the bad guys. So I did.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: And Shalmar, how come you've brought Apple with you? Isn't she supposed to be at home guarding the house?

dialogues.speaker: Shalmar
dialogues.text: Apple was worried about you, so she came along. You know she only listens to you and your mom. There's no way I can persuade her to go back home.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Banu seems to know that Rishboland Tiger jumping out of nowhere... Did she just call it Apple...? And that man showing up with that tiger... Ohh, Paimon's got a million questions...

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: Ahem, please allow me to introduce...

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: This klutz here is Shalmar, author of 50 Things Every Traveling Scholar Should Know, the book that I lent you.

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: I meant to introduce both Shalmar and Apple to you after the summoning ceremony of the Great Future Star. But just as I expected, something unexpected happened.

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: Well, at least we won't have to go looking for them. This accident was certainly unexpected, but it wasn't bad at all! If only I could be this lucky next time as well...

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: Good day, I'm Shalmar, Banu's biological father.

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: As for Apple, she's a graceful female Rishboland Tiger, and also a significant member of our family.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: B—Biological father? What's that supposed to mean...? Are you not Banu's father in other respects?

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: That is correct. From my perspective, Banu and I share an equal friendship, while in everyday life, we are teammates, people who have divided the household chores between us.

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: Being a father is but the very most insignificant of my identities, and I much prefer being her friend to being her father.

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: I have been listening to your conversation just now, all while hiding in that hole in the ground right beneath the mechanism. Now that I have heard how willing you are to help Banu, I must extend my gratitude to you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're welcome.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, this overly formal way of speaking... No wonder Banu talked to us like that when we first met...

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: Her phrasing and way of doing things are indeed similar to my own, but even as a child, I would say that Banu is a much more impressive person overall.

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: For example, the mixed rice she makes is 10,000 times better than the one I make. That alone is superb enough.

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: Therefore, I cherish dearly my time spent with such a happy, lively, and marvelous child.

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: Whenever I think of her going to the Akademiya, pulling her hair out till midnight every day in the library, suffering from malnutrition due to irregular meal timings over long periods of time, and her hair turning white even before she turns 40...

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: It pains me beyond description.

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: So naturally, before she starts a new life in the Akademiya, I must seize every opportunity to create as many fun memories for her as I can. This "Star-Seeker's Sojourn" was designed for this exact purpose as well.

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: Since I am somewhat acquainted with both Ley Lines and mechanics, I've made some special arrangements regarding the mechanisms around these parts.

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: Hey Shalmar, I gotta ask you this. Were you the one who called those monsters out — you know, when we were looking for the Future Stars, and just now too?

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: No, I would never! They... were all accidents. I only have myself to blame for having put you in danger, all because of my lack of consideration...

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: #I—I actually asked Apple to follow you in secret. As for this young adventurer, {M#he}{F#she} is apparently more than capable. So...

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: *sigh* You are really an unreliable father, you know? What would you ever do without me and Apple?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The two of us have been traveling for a long time, but we've never met a father as strange as you...

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: You believe me to be strange? Well, being strange is one of my key traits, so that was one of the best compliments I could possibly receive.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is that part of your setting, too?

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: Indeed so. Otherwise, what would the difference between me and the tides of human mediocrity in this overpopulated world be?

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: No matter how strange my words and deeds are, I nonetheless remain an ordinary person in this vast world, and yet I have the freedom to talk nonsense — something that those prestigious sages can only dream of.

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: Is that not such a delight?

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: Don't be fooled by him. Every time he tries to hide something, he'll act like this and start talking nonsense.

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: Anyway, Shalmar, where's my Great Future Star?

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: You said that collecting all six Future Stars and unlocking the final mechanism would bring the Great Future Star out. Where is it, then?

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: Relax, relax! I swear I wasn't deceiving you. Look, the Great Future Star is right here!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Shalmar takes out a Starconch from his pocket and hands it to Banu.

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: This is the Great Future Star — that which has crossed the vast sea of stars and come to you after you collected all the Future Stars. Look, doesn't it have a shining white star on its surface?

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: This Star is formed by all the Future Stars you've collected, and it is your very own Great Future Star. Put your ear to that black opening and listen carefully. Listen to the sea of stars as it speaks to you.

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: Ooh! So this is the Great Future Star!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's nonsense! This is just a Starconch! You can find them anywhere on the beaches of Liyue!

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: Oh... Well, Shalmar, is "Starconch" its alternative name in another setting?

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: Ahem... Yes, you can say that. In the settings that many people imagine, this is known as a Starconch, and it dwells in the sea. H—However, in the setting I have created, its name is the Great Future Star.

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: Ah, I get it. It's like that thing from the Akademiya's dumpster! I call it "Banu's Wisdom," but everyone else calls it "Ayesha's Chaos Prospector."

response.speaker: Banu
response.text: Thank you, Shalmar. I love the Great Future Star very much!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, are we just going to muddle our way through like that?

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: I wouldn't call this "muddling," exactly. Everyone perceives the world in their own way. And in my very own eyes, this is indeed the Great Future Star that has traveled across the sea of stars to arrive here.

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: Isn't it fun to tap into new ways of seeing the world? Plus, Banu has accepted the name as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Tap into new ways of seeing the world? Hmmm... So, {NICKNAME}, should we start seeing the Mints in your bag as Mora?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon, please tell me you didn't fall for that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon just thought it would make our journey much more lighthearted, y'know?

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: Please rest assured, the two of you. Even I would never utter nonsense when it comes to Mora. I ensure you that you'll be duly paid and that this commission will be worth your while.

response.speaker: Shalmar
response.text: Please take these as your rewards. Thank you for taking care of Banu for the past few days. Your good deeds shall be remembered forever.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey {NICKNAME}, don't be fooled! What if you started perceiving Mora as something trivial? Wouldn't you start throwing them away, then!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, that's a hard no for sure!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This Shalmar guy is too good at talking his way out of things. We'd better bring up the rewards first before he tries to pull a fast one on us again!

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: I knew it wouldn't go that easily. Quick, let's hide here together!
Raargh!

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: It's Apple! She's here to help us! See that Rishboland Tiger? That's our Apple!

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: She's really strong, so don't worry — we're in good hands now. C'mon, Apple! Smash them!
